findings.claim: The plan makes a docs page due when 'a listed source changed', but also says kmctl new doc never writes verified and a missing verified does not make a page due. review_due measures a source change against the last verified date only (changed > verified_at, and nothing at all when verified_at is None). A docs page with no verified has no baseline, so as written the source-changed reason either never fires for any page kmctl creates, or fires forever for every page with a tracked source. The plan must name the baseline for an unverified docs page (for example the page's own last git commit) or drop the source-changed reason for such pages. r6 tests a contract the plan leaves undefined.

r11 runs pre-commit in a scratch repo that lists this checkout under repos:. pre-commit is not a dependency here (the repo uses prek via uvx), a remote python hook makes the tool clone a committed rev and pip-install kmctl and its deps from PyPI, and the worktree's .pre-commit-hooks.yaml is uncommitted when the gates run. A test that reaches the network would need the integration marker, but pyproject addopts deselects integration tests and r11's command does not pass -m integration, so it would select zero tests (pytest exit 5) or put a network install in the unit gate. Decide how r11 runs (which tool, committed copy of the tree, offline or marked integration with a matching command) before building. A spike can answer it: can prek (or pre-commit) install and run a language: python hook from a local path repo, from a temporary commit, offline or within the gate timeout?

The plan makes the root-index finding a warning 'so a downstream repo's CI stays green after an upgrade', but a missing folder index is an error. Every downstream repo with docs/ pages has no folder indexes today, so bumping the action ref (it installs kmctl from action_path) turns its CI red until someone runs kmctl update or kmctl check --fix. Either that is intended and the plan should say so (an operator acceptance under 'Could invalidate this plan' and a line in the ADR and upgrade docs), or a missing folder index must also be a warning. As written the stated goal and the error level contradict each other.
Unverified docs pages had no baseline for "a listed source changed".
The pre-commit hook test could not run offline and selected no test under the integration marker.
A missing folder index as an error turns downstream CI red on upgrade, against the reason for the root warning.

This repo's docs-layout rule keeps the old sentence next to the new one: 'Its index page, README.md at the top of docs/, lists every page. Its index page, README.md at the top of docs/, links each folder's own README.md index'. The first sentence is now false and contradicts the second. The shipped claude and antigravity copies got it right.

Row r7's fails_when includes 'a page with no front matter fails', but neither field_shape test has a page without front matter: test_field_shape_good_and_absent_pass overwrites upgrade.md with full front matter, and install.md has a description. The name says 'absent' but no absent case is checked. Other tests (check_fix) cover it indirectly, but not the row's command.

The tutorial still says every command was run with kmctl 0.1.0 and the output is what it printed, but the new check / check --fix output (warning level, 'fixed', '1 failed, 1 warning') only exists from this change on.
